CATEGORY: formal words and register (Vocabulary (word choice))
definition: Choose words that fit the register of the sentence; some words are formal, conversational, or used only in a particular context.

HER NOTES IN THIS CATEGORY (4 distinct):
1 | “真” is usually used in conversation
1 | 本+N. is usually used in formal advertisement/news, also it indicates the author owns the tree, which is not the fact: the author is a pear, who does not own the whole pear tree. 爬上这棵树。
1 | “使” is more formal and better fit other formal words like “失业
1 | “却” indicates unexpected semantic turn

HER CORRECTIONS (4 of 4):
[mengmu_samples#35/f4/p0/k0/e0] 墓地的人[真→很]影响孟子  || her note: “真” is usually used in conversation
[pear_story#4/f3/p0/note/e0] 他这个没有礼貌的人每天爬上⟦本树⟧  || her note: 本+N. is usually used in formal advertisement/news, also it indicates the author owns the tree, which is not the fact: the author is a pear, who does not own the whole pear tree. 爬上这棵树。
[pear_story#4/f23/p0/k0-1/e4] 但政府实行的改革经济一系列政策⟦就让⟧他失业  || her note: “使” is more formal and better fit other formal words like “失业
[pear_story#4/f23/p0/k0-1/e2] 但政府实行的改革经济一系列政策[就让→却使]他失业  || her note: “却” indicates unexpected semantic turn

output.rule: Choose words that fit the sentence’s register and meaning: 真 is usually conversational, while 使 fits formal words such as 失业; 本+N. is usually formal advertisement/news language and can imply ownership, and 却 indicates an unexpected semantic turn.
output.explanation_template: <wrong> → <correct>: <wrong> is <conversational/formal/ownership-implying> here, while <correct> fits the <formal register/meaning/context>; use 却 only for an unexpected semantic turn.

examples.explanation: 真 → 很: 真 is usually used in conversation, while 很 fits this narrative sentence.
本树 → 这棵树: 本+N. is usually formal advertisement/news language and implies that the author owns the tree; 这棵树 fits the context.
就让 → 使: 使 is more formal and fits the formal word 失业.
就让 → 却使: 却 indicates an unexpected semantic turn, and 使 fits the formal register of 失业.

output.not_an_error: Do not flag 却 merely because it is formal; use it when there is an unexpected semantic turn. Do not use 本+N. when it would incorrectly imply that the author owns the noun.
